websiteToolRpeChart.title: RPE and RIR chart with load calculator
websiteToolRpeChart.intro: A chart of what share of your one-rep max each number of reps is at each RPE, what RPE means in reps left, and a calculator that turns a set you did into the load for another set.

chart.title: Share of your one-rep max
chart.note: Read across for the reps you do and down for the effort you rate the set. 100% is the one-rep max itself.

meaning.title: What each RPE means
meaning.none: No reps left. The set ended at failure.
meaning.one: One rep left in the tank.
meaning.two: Two reps left in the tank.
meaning.three: Three reps left in the tank.
meaning.four: Four reps left in the tank.

problems.weight: Enter the weight you lifted as a number above 0.
problems.reps: Enter the reps as a whole number from 1 to 10.
problems.targetReps: Enter the target reps as a whole number from 1 to 10.

results.targetRounded: Rounded for a bar with standard plates
results.roundedNote: Rounded to the smallest steps a bar loaded with standard plates goes up in. Without a gym the app uses the same steps.

sections.title: What RPE means
body: RPE, rate of perceived exertion, runs from 1 to 10. A set rated 10 had no reps left. RPE 9 left one rep in reserve, RPE 8 two, and so on.
Reps in reserve (RIR) is the same scale written the other way: RPE = 10 minus RIR. The Musclog app stores a set's effort either way, and the two are the same number.

sections.title: Why people misjudge it
body: Judging how many reps you had left is a skill, and most people are less accurate the further a set was from failure. A set that felt like it had a few reps left may have had more or fewer.
Treat the chart as a guide. Check it against how your sets actually go, and rate effort honestly when you log it.

sections.title: How the chart and calculator work
body: Each cell is the share of your one-rep max that many reps at that RPE represent. It comes from the same averaged formulas the Musclog app uses to estimate a logged set.
The calculator estimates your one-rep max from a set you did, then gives the load for a different number of reps at a different RPE. The rounded load is what a bar with standard plates can make.

sources.zourdos: Zourdos et al. (2016), Novel resistance training-specific RPE scale measuring repetitions in reserve
